key_insight: Overlapping domain decomposition in FBPINNs creates block-sparse derivative structure that makes Gauss–Newton optimization more scalable.
engineering_relevance: Exploiting this sparsity can reduce derivative computation and memory costs when training neural PDE solvers for multiscale engineering problems.
method: Identify block sparsity in the residual Jacobian and Gauss–Newton matrix from localized subnetworks.
Use graph-colored sparse automatic differentiation to compress derivative evaluations while retaining structurally nonzero entries.
Assemble block-sparse Gauss–Newton systems for sparse direct or preconditioned iterative solution.
evidence_signal: Multiscale PDE experiments report high accuracy and substantially faster optimization than first-order baselines, but the abstract provides no numerical speedups or problem sizes.
watch_item: Practical scalability depends on subdomain overlap, coloring overhead, and sparse linear-solver performance.
paper_title: Block-Sparse Gauss-Newton Optimization of Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Sparse Automatic Differentiation Approach
